chief_complaint: severe scar contracture across anterior neck limiting head extension 1 year after thermal burn injury
hpi_details: 44M status post deep partial and full-thickness thermal burns to neck and chest 1 year ago managed with split-thickness skin grafts. Presents with a thick, tight, fibrous scar band across his anterior neck that pulls his chin downward toward his sternum (mentosternal burn scar contracture). Complains of inability to look upward, tightness when swallowing, and difficulty turning his head while driving.
ideas: thinks the thick scar band is pulling his jaw permanently out of alignment
concerns: worried he will choke or never be able to extend his neck normally again
expectations: wants surgical release of the tight band and scar revision to restore his neck movement
pmh: History of 20% TBSA burns healed with grafting

clinical_knowledge.topic: Post-burn scar contracture evaluation and reconstructive management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of post-burn scar contracture is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Schedule for surgical scar contracture release utilizing multiple Z-plasties (to reorient the scar vector by 90 degrees and recruit adjacent lax tissue) or thick split-thickness / full-thickness skin grafting if defect after complete incisional release is extensive, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: severe scar contracture across anterior neck limiting head extension 1 year after thermal burn injury

Key HPI features: 44M status post deep partial and full-thickness thermal burns to neck and chest 1 year ago managed with split-thickness skin grafts. Presents with a thick, tight, fibrous scar band across his anterior neck that pulls his chin downward toward his sternum (mentosternal burn scar contracture). Complains of inability to look upward, tightness when swallowing, and difficulty turning his head while driving.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 76, BP 130/82. Neck examination reveals a dense, linear and webbed hypertrophic scar contracture band spanning from the submental region to the manubrium. Active and passive cervical extension limited to 15 degrees past neutral (normal 60 degrees). Pulling on the scar band blanches the surrounding skin and distorts the lower lip downward. Underlying tracheal cartilage anatomy palpable and intact.
Relevant background/PMH: History of 20% TBSA burns healed with grafting
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out a functionally significant post-burn scar contracture.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing the restriction exclusively to hypertrophic scarring without assessing the functional contracture and reconstructive options.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: new breathing or swallowing difficulty from neck tethering, or an anticipated difficult airway because cervical extension is mechanically restricted.
management_principles: Schedule for surgical scar contracture release utilizing multiple Z-plasties (to reorient the scar vector by 90 degrees and recruit adjacent lax tissue) or thick split-thickness / full-thickness skin grafting if defect after complete incisional release is extensive
Post-operative regimen must include custom thermoplastic neck extension splinting worn 24 hours/day and aggressive scar massage with silicone gel sheeting to prevent re-contracture
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 44M presenting with mature anterior neck burn scar contracture causing severe mechanical restriction of cervical extension and rotation.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 76, BP 130/82. Neck examination reveals a dense, linear and webbed hypertrophic scar contracture band spanning from the submental region to the manubrium. Active and passive cervical extension limited to 15 degrees past neutral (normal 60 degrees). Pulling on the scar band blanches the surrounding skin and distorts the lower lip downward. Underlying tracheal cartilage anatomy palpable and intact.
reference_soap.assessment: Severe Anterior Neck Burn Scar Contracture (Linear/Webbed band deformity).
reference_soap.plan: Refer to a burn-reconstruction team for functional assessment and shared planning. Contracture release and the choice of local rearrangement or grafting depend on scar extent, available tissue, airway/swallowing function, and patient goals. Splinting, therapy, scar care, and follow-up should be individualized by the treating team to reduce recurrence.

learning_objectives: Explain the geometric principles and angles of Z-plasty local tissue rearrangement in breaking up linear scar bands and lengthening contractures
Differentiate hypertrophic scars (staying within boundaries of original wound) from keloids (extending beyond original wound boundaries into normal skin)
Understand the biomechanical necessity of prolonged post-operative static splinting and pressure garment therapy following burn scar contracture release
Outline options for reconstructive coverage after contracture excision (local transposition flaps vs full-thickness skin grafts vs free tissue transfer)

teaching.one_liner: A mature, tight scar band left by a healed deep burn that mechanically tethers the chin to the chest — an elective reconstructive problem, not acute burn care.
red_flags: New breathing or swallowing difficulty from neck tethering
Rapidly worsening pain, redness, warmth, drainage, or fever suggesting infection

must_ask.say: When did the neck scar begin to tighten, and how quickly has movement become limited?
Can you look up normally, swallow comfortably, and breathe without the scar pulling?
Is the scar becoming more painful, red, warm, swollen, or draining fluid, and have you had a fever?
What stretching, splinting, therapy, silicone, or previous surgery have you tried?
What activities are most limited, and do you smoke or have medical conditions that could affect healing?

history.answer: A thick burn scar across my neck is pulling so tight that I can barely lift my chin or look up.
The scar started tightening about six months after my skin grafts healed, and it has gradually become thicker and stiffer over the past several months.
It runs right down the middle of my neck, from directly under my chin straight down to the top of my breastbone.
It feels like a tight, rigid cable holding my head down, and I can only tilt my neck up a tiny bit before it stops me.
It progressively tightened over the last six months, but recently it feels like it has set in completely and stopped stretching at all.
Trying to look up, turning my head to check blind spots, or looking up at high machinery pulls painfully on my neck and lower lip.
Keeping my head tilted slightly downward eases the tension, but nothing really loosens or softens the tight band.
I feel a tight, tugging sensation in my throat whenever I swallow large bites of solid food, but food does not get stuck.
No, my breathing is completely normal, and I don't feel short of breath or hear any wheezing.
No, my voice sounds completely normal and I have not had any hoarseness.
It occasionally itches along the thick edges, and it aches when I try to stretch my neck, but there is no sharp pain at rest.
No, there is no redness, swelling, warmth, pus, open sores, or fever.
Exactly one year ago, a high-pressure steam pipe ruptured at my factory and burned my neck and upper chest.
I was hospitalized at a burn center for four weeks and received split-thickness skin grafts on my neck and chest.
I wore a neck collar and compression garment for six months and applied moisturizing silicone gel, but the tight band still formed.
No, I have never had any radiation treatments to my head or neck.
I cannot turn my head properly to check blind spots while driving, and at work I have to bend my entire back just to look up.
I am worried that this thick cord is pulling my lower jaw and teeth permanently out of alignment.
I am terrified that it might eventually choke off my breathing or that my neck will be stuck pointing down permanently.
I want to have surgery to release this tight band and fix the scar so I can move my head freely again.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or heart disease.
Aside from the burn debridement and skin grafting surgeries one year ago, I have never had any other operations.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I drink one or two beers on weekend evenings, but nothing heavy.
I work as a factory supervisor and live at home with my wife and teenage son.
My father has mild high blood pressure, but there is no family history of abnormal scarring or keloids.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 130/82 mmHg, heart rate is 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, body temperature is 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
Well-appearing adult male in no acute distress, sitting comfortably with his head held in slight forward neck flexion.

A dense, linear, webbed hypertrophic scar contracture band spans from the submental region to the sternal manubrium, with surrounding skin blanching and downward distortion of the lower lip upon tension; underlying tracheal cartilage anatomy is palpable and intact without erythema or drainage.
Active and passive cervical extension is severely limited to 15 degrees past neutral due to firm soft tissue tethering, with moderate mechanical restriction during lateral rotation bilaterally.
Oral mucosa is moist and pink, uvula is midline, dentition is stable, and lower lip displays passive downward traction when extending the neck.
Breath sounds are clear and equal bilaterally with no stridor, wheezes, or crackles.
